title: dactylis glomerata subsp. lobata
intro: Dactylis glomerata subsp. lobata, commonly known as Cock's-foot or Wood Meadow-grass, is a type of grass that belongs to the family Poaceae. It is native to Europe and Western Asia, and has been traditionally used for its medicinal properties. The plant is known for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, which make it beneficial for health issues such as digestive problems, wounds, and skin conditions. The bioactive constituents of Dactylis glomerata subsp. lobata include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and saponins, which contribute to its therapeutic actions, including analgesic, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial effects.
